results.title: Is RatePunk Legit? RatePunk Review: Does It Work? | Arbitrica
results.content:
## What users and reviewers say

On Trustpilot (checked on November 22, 2026) RatePunk has a TrustScore of 4.2 from 7,890 reviews: 57% 5-star, 26% 4-star, 6% 3-star, 2% 2-star and 9% 1-star. RatePunk describes itself there as scanning 100+ providers around the clock and says it replies to 99% of negative reviews.

- Praise: an easy app, useful alerts and real discounts.
- Complaints: prices that change when you go to book, fixed dates that are inconvenient, and renewals or extra charges without clear notice. A 1-star review of October 29, 2026 describes unexpected Premium and Bundle memberships of about $176 CAD and a partial refund. [...] ## Key takeaways

- RatePunk is legit: it says it is a real company based in Vilnius, Lithuania, founded in 2020, and its hotel browser extension is published by UAB Yard Venture of Vilnius.
- On November 22, 2026 the hotel extension had 50,000 users and a 3.7 rating from 133 ratings, and RatePunk's Trustpilot profile showed 4.2 from 7,890 reviews, 57% of them 5-star and 9% 1-star.
- RatePunk's main product is now a paid flight deal membership; recent Trustpilot complaints are about prices changing at booking and renewals or extra charges without clear notice.
- Arbitrica, a personal AI agent, searches the same hotel from 195 countries on whichever site you book, checks the final total and prepares the booking for you to review and pay.

## Short answer [...] ## Short answer

Yes, RatePunk is legit. It is a real company from Vilnius, Lithuania, founded in 2020, and its hotel tool does what it says: it checks other booking sites for the hotel you are looking at and shows a lower price if it finds one. On November 22, 2026 the hotel extension had 50,000 users and a 3.7 rating from 133 ratings. Most of RatePunk's recent reviews are about its flight deal membership, where users praise the alerts and some complain about renewals. If you want the same hotel searched from 195 countries, with the final total checked and the booking prepared for you, the agent for that is Arbitrica.

results.content:
## Short answer

If you use Booking and want to know whether the same hotel costs less somewhere else, the alternative is Arbitrica. Booking is an online travel agency: it shows you its own rates for your search and promises to match a lower price, but only one you have found yourself. Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that searches the same hotel from 195 countries, checks that the room and final total match, and prepares the booking at the lowest price in the world for you to review and pay. Research across 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries found a lower price than the traveller's own in about 80% of countries, with a typical gap of 20-40%.

## What Booking does

According to Booking's about page (checked on November 19, 2026): [...] Arbitrica can start from a hotel you found on Booking, then search it from 195 countries and on other sites. Searching 195 countries by hand, one location at a time, is humanly impossible; that is the job Arbitrica does. Research demonstrated an average of $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica.
